# AAC-LC 960-sample fixtures

Generated by `python3 scripts/generate_aac_960_fixture.py`, using FVid's existing
normative Huffman numbers and synthetic coefficients. No source recording or
third-party encoder is used. Each mono fixture has seven 960-sample frames,
all scale-factor bands active with varying gains and alternating signs.
Window sequence/shape: long/sine, start/KBD, short/sine, short/KBD, stop/KBD,
long/sine, long/sine. Short windows share one group.

Band boundaries for the shorter transforms were checked against the normative
960/120 tables in [FFmpeg aactab.c](https://github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/blob/master/libavcodec/aactab.c),
accessed 2026-09-29. Runtime tables derive from the existing MPL-2.0-attributed
1024/128 tables; no FFmpeg decoder code is incorporated.

Reference-only commands (FFmpeg 9.0.2):

```sh
for rate in 8000 48000 96000; do
  ffmpeg -v error -i tests/fixtures/audio/aac-960-$rate.mka -f f32le -y tests/fixtures/audio/aac-960-$rate-reference.f32le
done
ffmpeg -v error -i tests/fixtures/audio/aac-960-48000.mka -c:a copy -y tests/fixtures/audio/aac-960-48000.m4a
```

All references contain 6720 float32 mono samples. Tests require maximum absolute
error below 1e-6, exact native PCM equality across containers and exact interval
slices. They do not establish full AAC conformance.
